briefdescription.para: Root shell document for the CloudAvid File Portal single-page application (SPA).

sect2.title: 🧒 ELI5 Summary
sect2.para: Imagine you have a really nice picture frame that never changes. The frame has a pretty top piece (the navigation bar with the logo), a pretty bottom piece (the footer with the company name), and a big empty space in the middle. Every time you want to show a different picture, you just swap the picture in the middle — you never throw away the frame! This file IS that frame. It's the one-and-only HTML page that your browser ever loads. All the "pages" you see (Home, Browse, etc.) are really just different pictures being slotted into the middle of this frame by JavaScript.

listitem.para: SPA Shell: Serves as the single, persistent HTML document; the browser never performs a full-page navigation away from this file.
Asset Pipeline Bootstrap: Loads every external resource the application needs — fonts, design-token CSS, component CSS, page-specific CSS, and the favicon — in the correct dependency order.
Persistent Chrome: Renders the navigation bar (<nav>) and footer (<footer>) once; they survive all client-side route transitions.
Content Mount Point: Provides <main id="app"> as the sole DOM node the client-side router targets for injecting/swapping page content.
Script Orchestration: Loads five JavaScript modules (i18n, banner, home, browse, router) in dependency order at the bottom of <body> so the DOM is fully parsed before any script executes.
Internationalization (i18n) Hooks: Sprinkles data-i18n attributes on translatable text nodes so the i18n module can find and replace them at runtime.
Progressive Enhancement of Language Toggle: Embeds an inline SVG globe icon inside #langBtn so the language-switch button is immediately styled without waiting for an icon font or sprite sheet.

sect1.title: 🏗️ Architectural Flow (DOT Diagram)
sect1.para: The diagram below visualises how the browser processes this file from the initial HTTP response through to an interactive, routed SPA.

sect1.title: 🔄 Execution Sequence (PlantUML Diagram)
sect1.para: This sequence diagram shows the runtime lifecycle from the moment the browser requests index.html to the first interactive paint.

sect2.title: Block 1 — DOCTYPE Declaration
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Forces the browser into standards mode so every CSS box-model calculation, layout algorithm, and rendering behaviour follows the W3C specification rather than legacy "quirks mode" heuristics.
🧒 ELI5: It's like telling the referee "we're playing by the official rules" before the game starts, so nobody argues about what's fair.

⚙️ Technical Details: <!doctype html> is the shortest valid doctype for HTML5+. It carries no version number or DTD URI because HTML is now a "living standard." Without it, Internet Explorer and some older engines fall back to quirks mode where width includes padding+border (IE5 box model), percentage heights resolve differently, and <table> font inheritance breaks.
📥 Inputs: None — this is a parser directive, not a DOM element.
📤 Outputs: Browser rendering mode set to "no-quirks."

sect2.title: Block 2 — <html> Root Element
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Establishes the document's language (en) and text direction (ltr), informing screen readers, search engines, and CSS logical properties how to interpret and render content.
🧒 ELI5: This is the big box that holds everything. The labels on the box say "English" and "read left-to-right" so everyone knows which way to read.

listitem.para: lang="en" enables correct hyphenation (hyphens: auto), tells assistive technologies which speech-synthesis profile to load, and helps Google determine the page's primary language.

dir="ltr" sets the base directionality for the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (UBA). When the i18n module switches to Farsi, it can flip this to dir="rtl", which cascades to every descendant via CSS logical properties (margin-inline-start, etc.).

sect2.para: 📥 Inputs: None.
📤 Outputs: Root element available to all scripts as document.documentElement.
🔗 Dependencies: The i18n.js module reads and mutates both lang and dir at runtime.

sect2.title: Block 3 — <head> Element (Container)
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Houses all metadata, style, and resource-hint declarations that the browser must process before it can begin layout and paint.

🧒 ELI5: Think of <head> as the instruction manual you read BEFORE you start building your LEGO set. It doesn't show you the LEGO pieces (that's <body>), but it tells you what tools and stickers you'll need.

⚙️ Technical Details: Everything inside <head> is non-visual. The browser constructs a parallel CSSOM (CSS Object Model) from the stylesheets listed here. Rendering is blocked until all render-critical CSS is downloaded and parsed. The <head> is parsed sequentially, which is why resource hints (preconnect) precede the actual font <link>.
📥 Inputs: None (opening tag).
📤 Outputs: Fully configured CSSOM, document title, favicon, and preconnected sockets.

sect2.title: Block 4 — Meta Charset Declaration
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Declares the character encoding as UTF-8, ensuring every glyph — from English letters to Farsi script (وزیرمتن) to emoji (☁️) — decodes correctly.
🧒 ELI5: This tells the browser which alphabet book to use. UTF-8 is the alphabet book that knows ALL the languages in the world, plus smiley faces!

⚙️ Technical Details: The HTML spec requires this meta tag to appear within the first 1024 bytes of the document. If absent or declared late, the browser performs encoding sniffing, which can cause a re-parse of the entire document and potential XSS vulnerabilities via charset mismatch attacks (e.g., UTF-7 injection).
📥 Inputs: None.
📤 Outputs: document.characterSet === "UTF-8".

sect2.title: Block 5 — Meta Viewport Configuration
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Instructs mobile browsers to set the layout viewport width to the device's screen width and the initial zoom level to 100%, enabling responsive design.

🧒 ELI5: Without this, your phone would try to show the entire website shrunk down to a tiny size like looking at a poster through binoculars held backwards. This tag says "show it at normal size, please!"

listitem.para: width=device-width maps the CSS px unit to the device-independent pixel (DIP) grid, making media queries like @media (max-width: 768px) fire at the expected breakpoints.
initial-scale=1 prevents iOS Safari from zooming out on landscape rotation. Note: maximum-scale=1 and user-scalable=no are intentionally omitted to preserve accessibility (pinch-to-zoom).

sect2.para: 📥 Inputs: None.
📤 Outputs: window.innerWidth matches CSS media query widths.

sect2.title: Block 6 — Document Title
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Sets the text displayed in the browser tab, bookmark list, and search engine results page (SERP) snippet.
🧒 ELI5: This is the name tag stuck on the browser tab so you can find this page when you have a million tabs open (we've all been there 😉).

⚙️ Technical Details: Format follows the Brand • Section pattern for SEO breadcrumb clarity. The bullet (•, U+2022) is a common separator that survives all encodings and renders cleanly at small tab-title font sizes. The router may update document.title on each route change for accessibility (screen readers announce title changes).
📥 Inputs: None.
📤 Outputs: document.title === "CloudAvid • File Portal".

sect2.title: Block 7 — Preconnect to Google Fonts API
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Opens an early TCP+TLS connection to fonts.googleapis.com so that when the browser encounters the font stylesheet <link>, the handshake is already complete, shaving 100–300 ms off font load time.
🧒 ELI5: Imagine you're ordering pizza. This step is like calling the pizza place ahead of time and saying "get the oven hot!" — so when you actually order, the pizza comes faster.

⚙️ Technical Details: rel="preconnect" performs DNS resolution, TCP handshake, and TLS negotiation. This is a non-blocking resource hint; if the connection isn't used within ~10 seconds, the browser may close it. This link targets the API server that returns the @font-face CSS, NOT the server that hosts the actual font binary files (that's fonts.gstatic.com, handled next).
📥 Inputs: None (resource hint).
📤 Outputs: A warm socket to fonts.googleapis.com.

sect2.title: Block 8 — Preconnect to Google Fonts Static CDN
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Opens an early TCP+TLS connection to fonts.gstatic.com — the CDN that serves the actual WOFF2/TTF binary font files. The crossorigin attribute is mandatory here because font files are fetched with CORS.
🧒 ELI5: The first call went to the pizza restaurant's phone line (Google API). This second call goes to the delivery driver's garage (Google Static) so he can start his car early.

⚙️ Technical Details: Without crossorigin, the browser opens a non-credentialed connection, but fonts are always fetched as anonymous CORS requests. This mismatch means the preconnected socket can't be reused, and the browser opens a second connection anyway — wasting the preconnect entirely. The crossorigin attribute (equivalent to crossorigin="anonymous") ensures the connection's credential mode matches the font fetch.
📥 Inputs: None (resource hint).
📤 Outputs: A warm, CORS-compatible socket to fonts.gstatic.com.

sect2.title: Block 9 — Google Fonts Stylesheet
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Fetches a dynamically generated CSS file from Google that contains @font-face declarations for four font families at the specified weight ranges, giving the application its distinctive typographic identity.
🧒 ELI5: This is like going to the sticker store and picking out four different fancy letter styles: one for titles, one for normal reading, one for Farsi text, and one for special headings.

entry.para: Primary sans-serif for body copy. Variable font, so a single file covers Regular through ExtraBold.
Persian/Arabic script support for RTL i18n.
Secondary geometric sans-serif, likely used for UI controls.

sect2.para: display=swap sets font-display: swap in every generated @font-face, meaning text is painted immediately with a fallback font and re-rendered once the web font arrives (FOUT rather than FOIT). This is optimal for Core Web Vitals (Largest Contentful Paint).
📥 Inputs: Preconnected sockets from Blocks 7 & 8.
📤 Outputs: Four font families available in the CSSOM; text renders with font-family: 'Manrope', … etc.
🔗 Dependencies: Consumed by tokens.css (custom properties like --font-body), which is loaded next.

sect2.title: Block 10 — Design Tokens Stylesheet
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Loads tokens.css, a file containing CSS custom properties (variables) that define the design system's primitive values: colours, spacing scale, font stacks, border radii, shadows, and breakpoints.

🧒 ELI5: This is the box of crayons. Before you draw anything, you pick which colours you'll use. tokens.css is where all the colour names live, like --color-primary (the blue crayon) and --space-4 (four steps wide).

⚙️ Technical Details: By loading tokens first, every subsequent stylesheet can reference var(--token-name) without worrying about cascade order. This follows the Design Token → Base → Components → Pages layering convention used by systems like Salesforce Lightning and IBM Carbon.
📥 Inputs: Font families from Google Fonts (Block 9) — tokens likely map --font-body: 'Manrope', sans-serif.
📤 Outputs: Custom properties on :root available to all downstream CSS.
🔗 Dependencies: Consumed by base.css, components.css, home.css, browse.css.

sect2.title: Block 11 — Base Stylesheet
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Loads base.css, which contains a CSS reset (e.g., *, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box }) and default element styles (typography, link colours, body background).

🧒 ELI5: Every browser has its own weird default look — some make bullet points big, some make headings a different size. base.css is like saying "everyone start from the same starting line" so the race is fair.

⚙️ Technical Details: Loaded after tokens.css so that reset rules can reference custom properties (e.g., body { font-family: var(--font-body); }). This layer should contain ZERO class selectors — only element, pseudo-element, and attribute selectors.
📥 Inputs: Custom properties from tokens.css.
📤 Outputs: Normalised default styles for all HTML elements.

sect2.title: Block 12 — Components Stylesheet
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Loads components.css, containing reusable, page-agnostic UI component classes such as .btn, .btn-sm, .btn-icon, .nav, .nav-bar, .nav-logo, .nav-actions, .footer, and .page.

🧒 ELI5: These are the LEGO instruction booklets for little builds — a button, a menu bar, a footer. You can use the same little build on any page, just like you can put the same LEGO car on any LEGO table.

⚙️ Technical Details: Components are styled with BEM-ish flat classes (.nav-logo-text, .nav-actions) rather than deeply nested selectors for specificity control and tree-shaking friendliness. This file must load before any page-specific CSS so that page overrides win by source order without needing !important.
📥 Inputs: Custom properties from tokens.css, reset from base.css.
📤 Outputs: Styled .btn, .nav, .footer, .page components.

sect2.title: Block 13 — Home Page Stylesheet
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Loads home.css, containing styles exclusive to the home/landing route (hero banner, feature cards, call-to-action sections, etc.).
🧒 ELI5: The Home page is the "welcome mat" of the website. This stylesheet picks the welcome mat's colour, pattern, and size.

⚙️ Technical Details: Although this is an SPA and not every route uses these styles, loading them upfront in <head> avoids a Flash of Unstyled Content (FOUC) if the user navigates to / and the styles haven't been fetched yet. For applications with many page-specific stylesheets, code-splitting via dynamic <link> injection would be preferable; for two pages (home + browse), upfront loading is the simpler, faster strategy.
📥 Inputs: Tokens, base, components.
📤 Outputs: Styles for home-page-specific DOM injected by home.js.

sect2.title: Block 14 — Browse Page Stylesheet
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Loads browse.css, containing styles exclusive to the file-browsing route (directory listings, file cards, breadcrumbs, grid/list toggle, etc.).
🧒 ELI5: The Browse page is like a library shelf view. This stylesheet decides how the books (files) are arranged — in a grid or a list — and what their spines look like.

⚙️ Technical Details: Same rationale as home.css above — loaded eagerly to prevent FOUC. The file likely uses CSS Grid or Flexbox for the directory listing layout and may include :empty or :has() states for empty-directory placeholders.
📥 Inputs: Tokens, base, components.
📤 Outputs: Styles for browse-page-specific DOM injected by browse.js.

sect2.title: Block 15 — Favicon
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Declares the page's favicon using a WebP image, displayed in the browser tab, bookmarks bar, and mobile home-screen shortcut.
🧒 ELI5: This is the tiny picture next to the page's name in the tab bar. It's like the little logo sticker on the spine of a book so you recognise it on the shelf.

⚙️ Technical Details: WebP is chosen over PNG for its superior compression (typically 25–35% smaller). Modern browsers universally support WebP favicons. The rel="icon" without a type attribute lets the browser sniff the MIME type from the HTTP response (image/webp). For legacy IE support (if needed), a /favicon.ico at the web root would be a fallback.
📥 Inputs: None.
📤 Outputs: Tab icon rendered.

sect2.title: Block 16 — </head> Closing Tag
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Signals the end of the document metadata section. The browser has now collected all information needed to construct the CSSOM and can begin processing the <body>.
🧒 ELI5: We've finished reading the instruction manual. Time to open the LEGO box!

⚙️ Technical Details: At this point the parser transitions from the "in head" insertion mode to "after head" and then "in body." The CSSOM from all five stylesheets plus Google Fonts has been (or is being) constructed. The render tree won't be built until both the DOM and CSSOM are ready.
📥 Inputs: All <head> children.
📤 Outputs: Parser state transition.

sect2.title: Block 17 — <body> Opening Tag
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Opens the document body — the container for all visible content.
🧒 ELI5: This is where we start placing the LEGO bricks on the baseplate. Everything from here on is stuff people can actually see and click on.

⚙️ Technical Details: The <body> element has no explicit class or id. Global page layout is delegated to the nested <div class="page"> wrapper, keeping <body> styling minimal (typically just margin: 0 from the reset in base.css).
📥 Inputs: CSSOM from <head>.
📤 Outputs: document.body reference available to scripts.

sect2.title: Block 18 — Page Layout Wrapper
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Wraps the entire visible page in a single <div> with class .page, providing a CSS layout context (likely display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-height: 100vh) that pushes the footer to the bottom even when content is short (sticky footer pattern).
🧒 ELI5: This is the picture frame that holds the top bar, the middle content, and the bottom bar together in a nice vertical sandwich.

⚙️ Technical Details: Using a .page wrapper rather than styling <body> directly provides:
A clean specificity boundary (class vs element selector).
A stacking context for potential z-index layering (modals, toasts).
The ability to add a max-width container or side padding without affecting body-level backgrounds or fixed-position elements.
📥 Inputs: None.
📤 Outputs: Flex column container for nav, main, footer.
🔗 Dependencies: Styled by components.css (.page class).

sect2.title: Block 19 — Navigation Bar
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Renders the persistent top navigation containing the logo, brand name, subtitle, external website link, and language toggle button. This element is never destroyed by the SPA router.

🧒 ELI5: This is the roof of our house — it's always there, no matter which room (page) you're standing in. It has the family name sign (logo), a doorbell to the main website, and a magic button that changes the language.

listitem.para: <nav class="nav"> — Semantic landmark element; assistive tech exposes it as a navigation role. The .nav class hooks into components.css for visual styling (backdrop blur, sticky positioning, z-index).
<div class="nav-bar"> — Inner flex container that horizontally distributes logo (start) and actions (end) with justify-content: space-between.

<a class="nav-logo" href="/" data-link> — The logo anchor navigates to the home route. data-link is a critical SPA attribute: the router intercepts clicks on any [data-link] anchor, calls history.pushState(), and re-renders #app instead of letting the browser perform a full page load.
— Company logo image. The alt text ensures screen readers announce the brand name.
<div class="nav-logo-text"> — Stacks brand name and subtitle vertically beside the logo image.
CloudAvid — The data-i18n="brand" attribute marks this node for translation by i18n.js. The text "CloudAvid" is the English fallback visible before the i18n module runs.
File Portal — Same i18n mechanism for the subtitle.
<div class="nav-actions"> — Groups the right-side controls.

Website — External link to the main website. btn btn-sm applies button-like styling at a small size. The text "Website" is translatable. Note: no data-link attribute, so this performs a normal navigation away from the SPA.

<button id="langBtn"> — Language toggle. btn-icon styles it as a square icon button. The title provides a tooltip and accessible name. Clicking it triggers the i18n.js module to cycle the locale (e.g., en ↔ fa), flip dir, and re-translate all [data-i18n] nodes.
The inline SVG is a globe icon from the Feather Icons set. Using inline SVG (rather than an or icon font) allows the icon to inherit currentColor for theming and eliminates an extra HTTP request.

sect2.para: 📥 Inputs: components.css for styling; i18n.js for translation; router.js for data-link interception.
📤 Outputs: Rendered nav bar with clickable logo, external link, and language toggle.

sect2.title: Block 20 — Main Content Mount Point
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: This empty <main> element is the sole injection target for the client-side router. Every route handler renders its HTML string into document.getElementById('app').innerHTML.
🧒 ELI5: This is the blank canvas in the middle of the picture frame. The robot painter (JavaScript router) keeps drawing new pictures on it every time you click a link, but the frame never moves.

listitem.para: <main> is a semantic landmark that assistive tech exposes as the document's primary content region. There should be only one <main> per document (spec recommendation).
id="app" is the contract between index.html and router.js. The router performs document.getElementById('app') to locate this node.
The element starts empty in the HTML source. Content appears only after router.js executes and matches the current URL to a route handler (e.g., home.js's render() or browse.js's render()).
Because the router replaces innerHTML, any event listeners attached to children of #app must either be re-attached after each render or use event delegation on #app itself.

sect2.para: 📥 Inputs: Rendered HTML from home.js, browse.js, or banner.js.
📤 Outputs: Visible page content between nav and footer.
🔗 Dependencies: router.js (write), home.js (content), browse.js (content), banner.js (content).

sect2.title: Block 21 — Footer
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Renders the persistent page footer with a copyright notice and a link to the company's main website. Like the nav, it is never destroyed by route changes.
🧒 ELI5: This is the bottom mat of the house — it always stays. It says "Made by CloudAvid" and has a link to visit them.

listitem.para: <footer class="footer"> — Semantic contentinfo landmark. The .footer class maps to components.css for styling (padding, border-top, flex row with justify-content: space-between).
© 2025 CloudAvid Co — Static copyright. Not marked data-i18n, so it appears unchanged in all locales. The year 2025 could be generated dynamically by JS if desired.
cloudavid.com — External link. No data-link because it navigates away from the SPA.

sect2.para: 📥 Inputs: components.css for styling.
📤 Outputs: Rendered footer at bottom of viewport.

sect2.title: Block 22 — Closing for .page
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Closes the .page layout wrapper opened in Block 18.
🧒 ELI5: We put the last side on the sandwich box. Snap!

⚙️ Technical Details: This terminates the flex column container. All three children (nav, main#app, footer) are now laid out. The main element typically gets flex: 1 in components.css so it absorbs remaining vertical space, pushing the footer to the bottom.
📥 Inputs: All children (nav, main, footer).
📤 Outputs: Completed flex layout.

sect2.title: Block 23 — Script: Internationalization Engine
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Loads i18n.js, the translation module that detects the user's locale, manages a dictionary of key→translation mappings, and replaces the textContent of every element bearing a data-i18n attribute.
🧒 ELI5: This is the translator friend who speaks both English and Farsi. When you press the globe button, they re-read every sign in the house and flip it to the other language.

⚙️ Technical Details: Loaded first among all scripts because other modules (banner.js, home.js, browse.js) may call i18n utility functions (e.g., t('key')) when rendering their templates. The module likely:
Reads localStorage or navigator.language for initial locale.
Sets document.documentElement.lang and .dir.
Exposes a global function or object (e.g., window.i18n or window.t()).
Attaches a click handler to #langBtn to toggle locales.
Walks the DOM to apply translations to all [data-i18n] elements.
📥 Inputs: DOM elements with data-i18n attributes; #langBtn.
📤 Outputs: Translated UI; lang/dir set on <html>.

sect2.title: Block 24 — Script: Banner Module
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Loads banner.js, which likely exports or registers a function to render a hero banner component into #app on the home route.
🧒 ELI5: This is the artist who paints the big "Welcome!" poster at the top of the home page.

⚙️ Technical Details: Loaded after i18n.js so it can use the t() function for translatable banner copy. It may export a renderBanner() function consumed by home.js, or it may register itself in a shared route-component registry.
📥 Inputs: i18n.js for translations; home.css for styling.
📤 Outputs: Banner HTML string or DOM fragment.

sect2.title: Block 25 — Script: Home Page Module
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Loads home.js, which defines the rendering logic for the home/landing route (/). It likely exports a render() function that returns an HTML string to be injected into #app.
🧒 ELI5: This is the instruction booklet for building the "Welcome Home" room inside our picture frame.

⚙️ Technical Details: The module probably:
Imports/uses banner.js's output as a sub-component.
Builds an HTML template with translatable strings via t().
Registers itself with the router (e.g., router.register('/', homeRender)), or the router imports its render function directly.
📥 Inputs: i18n.js, banner.js, home.css.
📤 Outputs: render() function for the / route.

sect2.title: Block 26 — Script: Browse Page Module
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Loads browse.js, which defines the rendering logic for the file-browsing route (e.g., /browse or /browse/:path). It likely fetches directory listings from an API and renders them as a file grid or list.
🧒 ELI5: This is the instruction booklet for building the "Library Shelves" room where you can see all the files and folders.

⚙️ Technical Details: The module probably:
Exports a render(path) async function that fetches a JSON directory listing from an API endpoint.
Constructs a DOM fragment with breadcrumbs, folder cards, and file cards.
Attaches click handlers (or uses event delegation on #app) for folder navigation via data-link anchors.
Supports query parameters for sort order, view mode (grid/list), etc.
📥 Inputs: i18n.js, browse.css, API data.
📤 Outputs: render() function for the /browse route.

sect2.title: Block 27 — Script: Client-Side Router
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Loads router.js, the last script, which initialises the client-side routing system. It reads the current URL, matches it to a registered route handler, and renders the corresponding page into #app.

🧒 ELI5: This is the traffic cop. When you click a link, instead of leaving the house and coming back, the traffic cop just tells the painter to change the picture in the middle of the frame. Much faster!

⚙️ Technical Details: Loaded last because it depends on all page modules (home.js, browse.js) being already registered/available. The module likely:
Defines a route table mapping URL patterns to render functions: { '/': homeRender, '/browse': browseRender, '/browse/:path': browseRender }.
Calls the initial render based on window.location.pathname.
Attaches a delegated click handler on document (or document.body) that intercepts clicks on any <a> with data-link:
event.preventDefault() — stops the browser from navigating.
history.pushState({}, '', href) — updates the URL bar.
Calls the matched route's render() and sets #app.innerHTML.
Listens for the popstate event (browser back/forward buttons) and re-renders accordingly.
May update document.title after each navigation for accessibility.
📥 Inputs: All page modules, #app DOM node, data-link anchors.
📤 Outputs: Live SPA navigation; content rendered in #app.

sect2.title: Block 28 — Closing </body> and </html>
sect2.para: 🎯 Purpose: Closes the document body and the root HTML element, signalling the end of the document to the parser.
🧒 ELI5: We've finished building everything. Time to close the LEGO box lid and admire our creation!

⚙️ Technical Details: When the HTML parser reaches </html>, it fires the DOMContentLoaded event (if not already fired). Since all <script> tags are non-defer/non-async and placed at the bottom of <body>, they execute synchronously before the parser reaches these closing tags. Therefore, DOMContentLoaded fires after all five scripts have executed, and the initial route has already been rendered into #app.
📥 Inputs: Fully parsed and scripted document.
📤 Outputs: DOMContentLoaded and eventually load events.

sect1.title: 📐 Conventions Table
sect1.para: The following table catalogues every custom attribute, ID, and CSS class used in index.html, along with the consuming module(s).

entry.para: Marks <a> tags for SPA client-side navigation (prevent default).
Translation key for the brand name ("CloudAvid").
Translation key for the subtitle ("File Portal").
Translation key for the website link text ("Website").
The sole DOM mount point for route-rendered content.
Language toggle button; i18n module attaches a click listener.
Full-height flex column wrapper (sticky footer pattern).
Inner horizontal flex container for nav content.
Logo anchor styling (flex row, gap, alignment).
Vertical stack for brand name + subtitle text.
Right-aligned group for nav action buttons/links.
Square icon-only button modifier (equal width/height, centred content).
Footer landmark styling (border-top, padding, flex row).
Current document language; mutated by i18n on locale switch.
Text directionality (ltr/rtl); mutated by i18n on locale switch.

simplesect.para: /assets/css/tokens.css — Design token custom properties (colours, spacing, fonts).
/assets/js/i18n.js — Internationalization engine with locale detection and DOM translation.
/assets/js/router.js — Client-side SPA router with History API integration.
